vectors.name: formats-json/basic/array-value-becomes-repeated-edges
vectors.comment: A JSON array is not a value in the Document model; it is the same label occurring more than once.

vectors.name: formats-json/basic/single-element-array-is-indistinguishable-from-a-bare-value
vectors.comment: {"m":[1]} and {"m":1} produce the identical one-edge Document -- there is no way to recover, from the Document alone, which spelling the source used.

vectors.name: formats-json/basic/empty-array-value-is-zero-edges-not-an-error
vectors.comment: An empty JSON array is a legitimate zero-edge encoding, not an error -- the label simply doesn't appear in the result. This does not extend to OML's [...] array sugar, where a bare m: [] MUST be rejected (verified live: 'empty array is not allowed') since a zero-length run is indistinguishable from no sugar at all; JSON's array is a real container independent of the edge-repetition mechanism, so an empty one carries meaning.

vectors.name: formats-json/basic/nested-array-is-rejected
vectors.comment: An array of arrays has inner elements with no label and therefore no edge to occupy; a reader MUST reject rather than flatten it.

vectors.name: formats-json/basic/date-looking-string-stays-a-string
vectors.comment: JSON has no temporal types, so a reader MUST NOT produce date/time/datetime on its own -- unlike YAML and TOML, this string only becomes a date if a schema upgrades it in stage 2.

vectors.name: formats-json/basic/repeated-edges-regroup-into-one-array-on-write
vectors.comment: The write-side complement of the array-becomes-repeated-edges parse vector above: two edges sharing a label regroup into one JSON array key regardless of what else might have separated them, since a JSON object cannot express cross-label interleaving (Sec7.3's grouping rule). Confirmed live.

vectors.name: formats-json/basic/temporal-leaf-is-stringified-on-write
vectors.comment: JSON has no temporal types; a writer MUST stringify a temporal leaf to ISO-8601 and report the adjustment. Confirmed live.

vectors.name: formats-json/basic/nan-substituted-with-null-and-reported
vectors.comment: NaN and Infinity are not valid JSON tokens; the default lenient mode substitutes null and reports the substitution rather than emitting invalid JSON. value:"NaN" is the vector-format's string-sentinel convention for this case (test-suite/README.md's canonical encoding section) -- JSON itself has no NaN token, so a vector can't hold one as an ordinary number without becoming invalid JSON itself. Confirmed live: severity is error, the one adjustment-family code that is (Sec8.3.8), since it actually changes the represented value, unlike the warning-severity adjustments.

vectors.name: formats-json/basic/cross-label-interleaving-lost-and-reported
vectors.comment: D-3 (closed 2026-08-23): Sec7.3's grouping rule already MUST group same-label edges regardless of position ([(m,A),(x,X),(m,B)] -> {"m":[A,B],"x":X}) -- no format in the JSON family (JSON/YAML/TOML) can express cross-label interleaving. What was missing was reporting the loss; format.interleaving-lost (Sec8.3.8) now MUST be emitted whenever a written Document actually had more than one distinct label AND at least one label's edges were not all contiguous, i.e. grouping changed relative order. Path is $, the whole document, since the loss isn't localized to one label's edges -- it's the interleaving between labels. This vector uses JSON as the representative case; the same MUST applies to YAML and TOML writers for the identical reason.
